ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Pulmonology Referral — Satchel Paige

code.originalText: Establishing primary care for two years of breathlessness on exertion and a morning cough: history, examination, blood tests including alpha-1 antitrypsin and eosinophils, ECG, NT-proBNP, cardiovascular risk, vaccines, a reliever inhaler and a pulmonology consultation

text.paragraph: Two years of breathlessness on exertion (mMRC 2) and a morning cough in a 73-year-old former smoker of about 30 pack-years, with a normal NT-proBNP and ECG. Please confirm or exclude COPD with spirometry interpreted with race-neutral equations, and advise on treatment, oxygen, rehabilitation and screening. [S]
Urgency: Routine, within two to three weeks. [S]

list.item: Does spirometry confirm COPD, and what is the severity when interpreted with race-neutral (GLI Global) reference equations?
What maintenance treatment do you advise, and is an inhaled corticosteroid indicated?
Given that pulse oximetry may overestimate his saturation, does he need an arterial blood gas, and does he qualify for long-term or ambulatory oxygen?
Is he a candidate for pulmonary rehabilitation and lung cancer screening?
What should his action plan and follow-up include?

text.paragraph: Breathlessness after one flight of stairs or a block on the level for about two years, gradually worse, with a morning cough and a little clear sputum most days; no exacerbation, hospital stay or course of steroids or antibiotics for his chest in the past year; no chest pain, orthopnea, ankle swelling, hemoptysis or weight loss. Former cigarette smoker of about 30 pack-years who stopped on his own eleven years ago. Retired professional pitcher; active and lean. No known allergy. Examination today: blood pressure 136/82, pulse 84, respiratory rate 18, oxygen saturation 94 percent on room air; prolonged expiration with reduced breath sounds; no crackles, wheeze, clubbing or edema. Results today: hemoglobin 15.2 g/dL, eosinophils 0.08 x 10^3/uL, alpha-1 antitrypsin 142 mg/dL, creatinine 1.08 mg/dL (eGFR 71 by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation), HbA1c 5.6%, NT-proBNP 92 pg/mL, LDL 148 mg/dL; ECG sinus rhythm, normal. CAT 18. Started today: albuterol with a spacer as needed and atorvastatin 20 mg; PCV20 and Tdap given. He wants his results explained to him and asked whether lung tests are scored differently for Black patients [S]

list.item: Breathless on stairs and on walks he used to take easily. [S]
He wants straight answers and his own numbers, and to be treated the same as anyone else. [S]
He wants to keep fishing and speaking to young people. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Leroy Robert Page was born in Mobile, Alabama, and was delivered at home by a midwife; his mother was a washerwoman and his father a gardener. The family later changed the spelling of the name to Paige. His accepted date of birth is July 7, 1906. [D]

His age was disputed for most of his career. He told stories that kept it uncertain, among them that his birth certificate had been kept in a Bible that the family goat ate; later he did not argue with the evidence for July 7, 1906. One historian suggests he was probably born earlier, with the date altered to make him more marketable. [R]

In 1918, at twelve, he was convicted of shoplifting and sentenced to five years in the Alabama Reform School for Juvenile Negro Law-Breakers, a segregated reform school; he was released at the end of 1923 and began his professional career soon after. [D]

Because organized baseball had excluded Black players since 1889, he spent his prime in the Negro leagues and on barnstorming tours from 1927 to 1947, pitching for clubs in Chattanooga, Birmingham, Baltimore, Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Kansas City. Black players on tour were barred from the hotels and restaurants used by white people, and he refused to play in towns where he could not get a room or a meal. [D]
In the late 1930s he developed arm trouble for the first time; after an arm injury in 1938 the Kansas City Monarchs signed him, and his arm recovered the following year. [D]

In July 1948, at 42, he made his major league debut for the Cleveland Indians, the oldest rookie in the major leagues, and helped them win the 1948 World Series. He pitched his last major league game for the Kansas City Athletics in 1965 at 59, and in 1968 joined the Atlanta Braves as a coach so that he could qualify for a major league pension. [D]
In 1971 he was the first Negro leagues player elected to the National Baseball Hall of Fame, as the first choice of its Committee on Negro Baseball Leagues. [D]
He married Janet Howard in 1934. He later married Lahoma Brown, and together they raised seven children in Kansas City, where he lived for most of his adult life. [D]
In his later years he had emphysema and heart trouble. [D]

list.item: Retired professional pitcher who starred for two decades in the Negro leagues, was kept out of the major leagues until 42 by the exclusion of Black players, pitched in the majors into his late fifties, and is in the Hall of Fame; still speaks at schools and community events [S]
Lives in Kansas City with his wife; seven grown children, several nearby [S]

Synthetic smoking history: smoked cigarettes from about 20, roughly three-quarters of a pack a day, about 30 pack-years, and stopped on his own eleven years ago; no vaping; no cannabis. A beer on a holiday (AUDIT-C 1) [S]
Walks to the corner store and back most days, stopping twice to catch his breath; used to fish; no stairs at home except the porch [S]

Grew up poor in segregated Mobile and spent five years of his boyhood in a segregated reform school; long experience of being barred from hotels and restaurants on the road; distrustful of being judged by race, and wants his care explained and his numbers shown to him [S]
Strengths: extraordinary physical discipline over a very long career, humor, a gift for storytelling, a close family and wide community respect [S]

Hyperlipidemia: LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 44 and triglycerides 160 at intake; estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk about 18 percent; atorvastatin started by shared decision: active, confirmed [S]

Breathlessness work-up at intake: symptoms with the CAT and mMRC, exacerbation history over the past year, smoking history and examination; blood count with eosinophils, alpha-1 antitrypsin once, kidney function, HbA1c, lipids, NT-proBNP and a 12-lead ECG; resting oxygen saturation read with care in darker skin. Guideline: Global Strategy for the Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2025 Report (2025); Race and Ethnicity in Pulmonary Function Test Interpretation: An Official American Thoracic Society Statement (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, COPD and hyperlipidemia monographs (2026) [S]
Albuterol with a spacer as needed for breathlessness, with technique checked at the visit. Guideline: Global Strategy for the Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2025 Report (2025) [S]

Cardiovascular risk: moderate-intensity atorvastatin by shared decision, with a lipid panel at about eight weeks; blood pressure at each visit; ECG reviewed after any exacerbation. Guideline: Global Strategy for the Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2025 Report (2025); Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication (2022) [S]

Vaccines: PCV20 and Tdap now; influenza, RSV and COVID-19 in the autumn; recombinant zoster. Guideline: Global Strategy for the Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2025 Report (2025); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026) [S]
Referral to pulmonology, Marcus Lindqvist-Bello, MD, ordered 2026-07-14 [S]
